description: Security control taxonomy. Categories map to cheatsheets by filename.

categories.name: Output Encoding and Context-Aware Escaping
categories.description: Encode or escape output for the target interpreter context (HTML elements, attributes, URLs, JavaScript, CSS) to prevent content from being misinterpreted as code. Includes canonical input decoding as a prerequisite.

categories.name: Rich Content Sanitization
categories.description: Sanitize user-supplied rich content (HTML from WYSIWYG editors, SVG, Markdown, CSS, BBCode) before rendering. Prevent dynamic code execution (eval) and template injection.

categories.name: Database and Query Injection Prevention
categories.description: Prevent injection into database queries (SQL, NoSQL, HQL, Cypher), directory services (LDAP), and XML queries (XPath). Use parameterized queries or equivalent safe APIs.

categories.name: Server-Side Injection Prevention
categories.description: Prevent injection into OS commands, LaTeX processors, regex engines, JNDI, memcache, format strings, SMTP/IMAP, and log systems. Covers all non-database, non-XSS interpreter injection.

categories.name: SSRF Prevention and Outbound Request Control
categories.description: Validate and restrict server-side outbound requests. Prevent SSRF through URL/protocol/domain allowlisting, blocking private IPs, and disabling automatic redirect following.

categories.name: Memory Safety, XML Parsing, and Deserialization
categories.description: Use memory-safe coding patterns (C/C++), configure XML parsers securely (disable external entities), and enforce safe deserialization with type allowlists.

categories.name: Input Validation Framework
categories.description: Define and enforce server-side input validation rules: structural validation, data format checking, cross-field consistency, and documented validation specifications.

categories.name: Business Logic Security and Anti-Automation
categories.description: Enforce business rules: sequential workflow processing, business limits, transactional integrity, resource locking, and rate limiting to prevent abuse.

categories.name: Cookie Security Configuration
categories.description: Configure all cookie security attributes: Secure flag, SameSite policy, __Host- prefix, HttpOnly for session cookies.

categories.name: HTTP Security Response Headers
categories.description: Configure security-related HTTP response headers: HSTS, CSP, CORS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, frame-ancestors, and correct Content-Type.

categories.name: CSRF and Cross-Origin Protection
categories.description: Prevent cross-site request forgery and cross-origin attacks via anti-forgery tokens, CORS preflight enforcement, safe HTTP methods, origin separation, and postMessage validation.

categories.name: API and HTTP Layer Security
categories.description: Secure HTTP message handling: redirect policies, trusted header verification, request smuggling prevention, IP forwarding header trust, and HTTP parameter pollution defense.

categories.name: GraphQL Security
categories.description: Secure GraphQL endpoints: disable introspection in production, enforce query depth limits, amount limits, and cost analysis to prevent resource exhaustion.

categories.name: WebSocket Security
categories.description: Secure WebSocket connections: enforce WSS (TLS), validate Origin header during handshake, use dedicated session tokens, and validate tokens via authenticated HTTP endpoints.

categories.name: File Upload, Storage, and Download Security
categories.description: Validate uploaded files (size, type, magic bytes, archive limits), store safely (prevent execution, path traversal), and serve securely (Content-Disposition, filename sanitization, antivirus scanning).

categories.name: Password Policy and Validation
categories.description: Implement modern password policy: minimum length, allow all characters, breach database checking, context-specific word blocking, no forced rotation, UI best practices (type=password, allow paste).

categories.name: Authentication Protection and Credential Lifecycle
categories.description: Protect authentication endpoints: brute force/credential stuffing prevention, remove default accounts, enforce consistent auth pathways, manage initial credentials, disable security questions, and secure password reset with MFA respect.

categories.name: Multi-Factor Authentication Implementation
categories.description: Implement MFA: require for L2, TOTP/lookup secrets/OOB codes with CSPRNG, one-time use, entropy requirements, code lifetime limits, OOB channel security, and brute force protection.

categories.name: Identity Provider and Federation Integration
categories.description: Securely integrate with external IdPs: namespace user IDs per IdP, validate assertion signatures, prevent SAML replay, verify authentication strength claims.

categories.name: Session Token Generation and Timeout Configuration
categories.description: Configure session management: server-side token verification, dynamic token generation with CSPRNG entropy, token regeneration on auth, inactivity and absolute timeouts.

categories.name: Session Termination and Abuse Prevention
categories.description: Ensure proper session termination on logout, account disable, and credential change. Enable user/admin session management. Require re-authentication for sensitive operations. Coordinate federated sessions.

categories.name: Authorization Enforcement
categories.description: Implement and enforce authorization at function, data-object, field, and tenant levels. Server-side enforcement with documented rules.

categories.name: JWT and Self-Contained Token Validation
categories.description: Validate JWTs/self-contained tokens: signature/MAC verification, algorithm allowlist, trusted key sources, expiry, type, audience, and issuer checks.

categories.name: OAuth Client and Resource Server Security
categories.description: Implement OAuth client correctly (PKCE, state/nonce, mix-up protection, token confinement) and configure resource server token validation (audience, scope, subject, auth strength).

categories.name: OAuth Authorization Server Configuration
categories.description: Configure the OAuth AS: redirect URI validation, authorization code lifecycle, grant restrictions, PKCE enforcement, refresh token management, client authentication, dynamic registration safety, scope limits.

categories.name: OIDC Client, Provider, and Consent Management
categories.description: Secure OIDC relying party (ID token replay/nonce, user identification, issuer validation, audience, back-channel logout), OpenID Provider (response modes, forced logout), and consent management.

categories.name: Cryptographic Configuration and Key Management
categories.description: Use approved algorithms, sufficient key sizes, crypto agility, authenticated encryption, CSPRNG, password hashing (Argon2id/bcrypt), and maintain crypto inventory with key lifecycle policy.

categories.name: TLS Configuration and Transport Security
categories.description: Configure TLS versions and cipher suites, mTLS validation, enforce HTTPS for all external and internal communications, and manage certificate trust.

categories.name: Secrets Management and Backend Service Authentication
categories.description: Set up secrets management, use service accounts with least privilege, eliminate default credentials, and document all backend communication needs.

categories.name: Production Deployment Hardening
categories.description: Remove debug modes, source control metadata, directory listings, HTTP TRACE, exposed internal endpoints, and test/sample code from production.

categories.name: Sensitive Data Classification and Protection
categories.description: Classify sensitive data, define protection requirements, keep sensitive data out of URLs, prevent server-side caching, block third-party leakage, set anti-caching headers, clear client-side data on logout.

categories.name: Defensive Coding Practices
categories.description: Apply defensive coding patterns: return only required fields, mass assignment protection, strict type checking, prototype pollution prevention, HTTP parameter pollution defense.

categories.name: Security Logging and Event Monitoring
categories.description: Configure structured security logging: metadata, timestamps, destinations, sensitive data handling, security event capture (auth, authz, control bypass), log protection, and secure log transport.

categories.name: Secure Error Handling
categories.description: Implement secure error handling: generic error messages (no stack traces/secrets), graceful degradation when external resources fail, fail-secure exception handling.

categories.name: WebRTC Security Configuration
categories.description: Secure WebRTC infrastructure: TURN server IP restrictions, DTLS certificate and cipher management, SRTP authentication and resilience, signaling server rate limiting and input validation.
